properties.reasoning: AACP-A-01 (Use-limited authorization survives a persistence boundary) is OBSERVED by probe P-A-01 and discriminates under repair M-04 (count token uses across committed batches as well as the pending buffer). Why this is A: A use limit carried by the authorization artifact is part of what makes it currently valid. For N = 1 the limit is single-use semantics, named verbatim in A's scope; an artifact accepted on use N + 1 is not currently valid.
properties.caveat: Boundary of AACP-A-01 is met: MaxExecutions is a caveat inside the signed CapabilityToken (message_to_sign covers caveats, lib.rs:76-81), so the limit belongs to the authorization artifact, not to a quota outside it. Token signature authenticity was not shown to fail: CapabilityToken::verify uses verify_strict over a canonical message and no forgery was attempted. Expiry, not-before and multi-process replay were not exercised. AACP-A-01 boundary: Applies only when the limit is part of the authorization artifact itself (for example a signed caveat). Quotas or rate limits enforced outside the artifact are not A; rate limiting is outside the model (SPECIFICATION §10). Also: P-A-02 (AACP-A-02, partial, cargo-test): OBSERVED, DISCRIMINATES, but the relationship is partial; P-A-03 (AACP-A-03, structural, cargo-test): OBSERVED, DISCRIMINATES, but the relationship is structural; S-A-04 (AACP-A-04, exact, source-check): OBSERVED by static source check only.

properties.reasoning: AACP-B-01 (Unauthenticated principal accepted) is OBSERVED by probe P-B-01 and discriminates under repair M-01 (require a request signature by the key registered for the actor). Why this is B: Actor identity is in B's scope. If the actor is taken from an unauthenticated field, the system cannot establish who held authority. AACP-B-02 (Principal key is self-attested) is OBSERVED by probe P-B-02 and discriminates under repair M-01 (require a request signature by the key registered for the actor). Why this is B: A key supplied by the request is bound to the request, not to the principal. Without a verifier-held principal-to-key binding, a valid signature does not establish who held authority. AACP-B-03 (Bearer authorization not bound to a subject) is OBSERVED by probe P-B-03 and discriminates under repair M-08 (bind the token to the requesting actor). Why this is B: Provenance of approved intent includes to whom authority was granted. An artifact usable by any requester carries no record of the principal it was issued to.
properties.caveat: Boundaries are met: NTI has no authenticated channel or principal-key registry on the evaluate() path, and has not declared bearer semantics for tokens as a non-claim. If it does, the AACP-B-03 part of this row becomes OUT_OF_SCOPE for the token path. Issuer provenance is partly enforced: a token needs a configured issuer key and a local grant for the capability; that was not shown to fail. Delegation chains do not exist in the assessed API. AACP-B-01 boundary: Not a failure if the actor is established by an authenticated channel on the mandatory path (for example mTLS identity mapped by the enforcement point); the probe must show the request is allowed with the actor field alone. AACP-B-02 boundary: Not a failure when the request-supplied key is itself certified to the principal by a trusted issuer that the verifier checks. AACP-B-03 boundary: A deliberately bearer design is a claim boundary. If the implementer states bearer semantics as a non-claim, the row is OUT_OF_SCOPE for that path, not FAIL. Also: S-B-03 (AACP-B-03, exact, source-check): OBSERVED by static source check only, DISCRIMINATES; S-B-04 (AACP-B-04, exact, source-check): OBSERVED by static source check only.

properties.reasoning: AACP-C-01 (Authorization not bound to the exact call) is OBSERVED by probe P-C-01 and discriminates under repair M-08b (bind the token to one call identity). Why this is C: Call identity, target and full argument binding are in C's scope. If the artifact the system accepts as sufficient to authorize execution binds none of them, the authorization is not bound to the exact call executed.
properties.caveat: Boundary of AACP-C-01 is met: probe P-C-01 sends no request signature, so the call is authorized by the token alone; the optional request signature is not on the mandatory path. If NTI declares tokens to be capabilities without call binding, this row becomes OUT_OF_SCOPE for the token path. The optional request signature covers id, actor, capability, action and input; argument substitution under a present, verified request signature was not attempted. Because that signature is optional and self-attested (row B), it does not establish exact-call binding. AACP-C-01 boundary: Not a failure when exact-call binding is enforced elsewhere on the mandatory path, for example a required request signature over the call recomputed at dispatch; the probe must show the call is allowed with the unbound artifact alone. A capability design that does not claim call binding is a non-claim (OUT_OF_SCOPE), not FAIL.

properties.reasoning: AACP-D-01 (Value constraint defeated by type confusion) is OBSERVED by probe P-D-01 and discriminates under repair M-05 (reject an amount that is not a non-negative integer). Why this is D: A value limit expresses what the authorized action may do in operational terms. Reading a disallowed value as zero, or ignoring its unit, permits an action outside that meaning. AACP-D-02 (Resource constraint not canonicalised) is OBSERVED by probe P-D-02 and discriminates under repair M-06 (component-wise prefix match and reject parent-directory components). Why this is D: A resource restriction is in D's scope. Matching the string rather than the resource it names permits actions on resources outside the authorized one. AACP-D-03 (Policy evaluated after the effect) is OBSERVED by probe P-D-03 and discriminates under repair M-13 (evaluate intent policies before dispatch). Why this is D: Expected effect and business intent are in D's scope. A policy on meaning that is evaluated only after the effect does not decide whether the action was permitted; it reports afterwards that it was not.
properties.caveat: Only two caveat types and one intent-policy path were exercised. P-D-03 shows the effect before the check with a real local file write; no payment or remote effect was produced. AACP-D-01 boundary: Not D when the limit is a syntactic schema check unrelated to the authorization; the limit must be part of what authorized the action. AACP-D-02 boundary: Not D when the restriction is not part of the authorization (for example a UI filter). AACP-D-03 boundary: Not a failure where the post-check is declared as detection only and a separate pre-dispatch check enforces the same policy; the probe must show the effect occurs in the system's fail-closed mode. Also: S-D-03 (AACP-D-03, exact, source-check): OBSERVED by static source check only, DISCRIMINATES.
